stem: In an \( L\text{-}C\text{-}R \) series circuit, \( R = 150\,\Omega \), \( L = 0.750 \) H and \( C = 0.0180\,\mu\text{F} \). If the source has voltage amplitude \( V = 150 \) V and a frequency equal to the resonance frequency of the circuit, then the average power delivered by the source is \( P \) watt. Now, the capacitor is replaced with \( C = 0.0360\,\mu\text{F} \) and the source frequency is adjusted to the new resonance value keeping all the other parameters constant. The average power delivered by the source now is;
reasoning: At resonance impedance = R, so P = V_rms^2/R, independent of L and C. Changing C then re-tuning to resonance gives the same power P. Answer (1) P watt. SOURCE DEFECT: options (2) and (4) render as bare 'Watt' - the leading coefficient/fraction (likely P/2 and P/4 distractors) failed to render in the source; transcribed verbatim as shown.
